title: Elasticity — 40 MCQs
description: Covers Hooke’s law, stress, strain, elasticity and plasticity, Young’s modulus, bulk modulus, shear modulus, Poisson’s ratio, energy stored in a stretched wire, and related numerical and conceptual problems.

questions.q: Hooke’s law states that within the elastic limit
options: stress is inversely proportional to strain
stress is directly proportional to strain
strain is proportional to the square of stress
questions.explanation: Hooke’s law asserts that stress ∝ strain provided the elastic limit is not exceeded; the constant of proportionality is the relevant modulus of elasticity.

questions.q: Stress is defined as
questions.explanation: Stress = F / A, where F is the deforming force and A is the area over which it acts.

questions.q: Strain is a
questions.explanation: Strain is the ratio of change in dimension to original dimension and therefore has no units.

questions.q: The property of a material by which it returns to its original shape after removal of the deforming force is called
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the ability of a body to regain its original configuration when the external deforming forces are removed.

questions.q: Plasticity is the property of a material by which it
options: regains original shape after removal of force
does not regain original shape after removal of force
questions.explanation: A plastic body retains the deformation permanently after the deforming force is removed.

questions.q: Young’s modulus is the ratio of
questions.explanation: Y = (F/A) / (ΔL/L) = F L /(A ΔL).

questions.q: Bulk modulus is defined as the ratio of
questions.explanation: B = −ΔP / (ΔV/V); the negative sign indicates that an increase in pressure decreases volume.

questions.q: Shear modulus (modulus of rigidity) is the ratio of
questions.explanation: η = (F/A) / θ, where θ is the shear strain (angle of shear in radians).

questions.q: Poisson’s ratio is defined as the ratio of
questions.explanation: σ = − (lateral strain) / (longitudinal strain); the negative sign indicates opposite sense of the strains.

questions.q: The SI unit of Young’s modulus is
questions.explanation: Young’s modulus has the same dimensions and unit as stress, i.e., N m⁻² or pascal.

questions.q: Within the elastic limit the graph of stress versus strain is
options: a straight line through the origin
questions.explanation: Hooke’s law implies a linear relationship between stress and strain up to the elastic limit.

questions.q: The energy stored in a stretched wire is
questions.explanation: Work done (and hence elastic potential energy) is the area under the force-extension graph, which is a triangle of area ½ F ΔL.

questions.q: Which of the following is a dimensionless quantity?
questions.explanation: Strain is a pure ratio of two lengths (or volumes) and is therefore dimensionless.

questions.q: The reciprocal of bulk modulus is called
questions.explanation: Compressibility κ = 1/B = −(1/V)(ΔV/ΔP).

questions.q: A wire of length L is stretched by ΔL. The longitudinal strain is
questions.explanation: Longitudinal strain = change in length / original length = ΔL / L.

The energy stored in a wire of length 1 m, area 2 mm² stretched by 1 mm under a force of 20 N is
If the length of a wire is doubled and its radius is halved, Young’s modulus of the material
questions.explanation: Young’s modulus is a material property and does not depend on the dimensions of the specimen.

questions.q: A rubber cord of length 10 cm and cross-section 1 cm² is stretched by 2 cm under a load of 50 N. The Young’s modulus is
The bulk modulus of a liquid is 2 × 10⁹ N m⁻². The pressure required to reduce its volume by 0.1 % is
Poisson’s ratio for a material is 0.25. If longitudinal strain is 4 × 10⁻³, the lateral strain is
questions.explanation: σ = lateral strain / longitudinal strain ⇒ lateral strain = 0.25 × 4 × 10⁻³ = 1 × 10⁻³.

questions.q: Two wires of the same material have lengths in the ratio 1 : 2 and radii in the ratio 2 : 1. The ratio of their elongations under the same load is
The work done in stretching a wire of length L, area A and Young’s modulus Y by an amount ΔL is
questions.explanation: U = ½ F ΔL and F = (Y A ΔL)/L, therefore U = (Y A (ΔL)²)/(2 L).

questions.q: A metal cube of side 10 cm is subjected to a shearing force of 4000 N. The top face is displaced by 0.05 cm relative to the bottom. The shear modulus is
If the stress–strain graph of a material is a straight line parallel to the strain axis, the material is
questions.explanation: A horizontal line means stress remains constant while strain increases indefinitely, which characterises a perfectly plastic material.

questions.q: The dimensional formula of modulus of elasticity is the same as that of
questions.explanation: Modulus of elasticity = stress/strain and strain is dimensionless, so it has the same dimensions as pressure (or stress).

questions.q: A wire of Young’s modulus 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻² is stretched by a force that produces a strain of 10⁻³. The energy stored per unit volume is
questions.explanation: Energy density = ½ × stress × strain = ½ × (Y × strain) × strain = ½ Y (strain)² = ½ × 2 × 10¹¹ × 10⁻⁶ = 10⁵ J m⁻³.

questions.q: For most metals Poisson’s ratio lies between
questions.explanation: Experimentally Poisson’s ratio for metals is typically between 0.25 and 0.4, and theoretically it cannot exceed 0.5 for isotropic materials.

questions.q: A steel wire and a copper wire of equal length and equal cross-section are joined end to end and loaded. The Young’s moduli are in the ratio 2 : 1. The ratio of their elongations is
questions.explanation: Under the same force and same A, ΔL ∝ 1/Y. Therefore ΔL_steel / ΔL_copper = Y_copper / Y_steel = 1/2.

questions.q: A wire of length 4 m and diameter 2 mm is stretched by 0.8 mm under a load of 20 N. The energy stored in the wire is
The pressure that can compress a liquid of bulk modulus 2 × 10⁹ Pa by 0.2 % is
Two wires A and B of the same material have radii in the ratio 2 : 1 and lengths in the ratio 1 : 2. When stretched by the same force, the ratio of stress in A to stress in B is
questions.explanation: Stress = F/A; A ∝ r² so stress_A / stress_B = (r_B / r_A)² = (1/2)² = 1/4.

questions.q: A rod of length 1 m and area 1 cm² is fixed at both ends. Its temperature is raised by 50 °C. If Y = 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻² and α = 1 × 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹, the thermal stress developed is
questions.explanation: Thermal strain = α ΔT = 5 × 10⁻⁴; thermal stress = Y α ΔT = 2 × 10¹¹ × 5 × 10⁻⁴ = 1 × 10⁸ N m⁻².

questions.q: The volume of a solid is decreased by 0.4 % when a pressure of 8 × 10⁷ Pa is applied. The bulk modulus of the solid is
A wire is stretched by 0.5 mm under a load of 10 N. The energy stored is 2.5 × 10⁻³ J. The extension under a load of 20 N (within elastic limit) is
questions.explanation: U = ½ F ΔL ⇒ 2.5 × 10⁻³ = ½ × 10 × ΔL ⇒ ΔL = 5 × 10⁻⁴ m = 0.5 mm for 10 N. Extension is proportional to load, so for 20 N, ΔL = 1.0 mm.

questions.q: A steel rod of length 1 m and area of cross-section 1 cm² is heated through 50 °C with ends clamped. Given Y = 2 × 10¹¹ Pa, α = 12 × 10⁻⁶ °C⁻¹, the tension produced is
If the work done in stretching a wire by 1 mm is 2 J, the work necessary to stretch the same wire by 3 mm (within elastic limit) is
questions.explanation: U ∝ (ΔL)². For ΔL → 3 ΔL, U → 9 U = 18 J.
